newsitem.title: USA: Alleged Cosby extortionists remain in jail.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Cosby extortionists remain in jail.

text.p: By Gail Appleson, U.S. Law Correspondent
A Los Angeles woman and an alleged male accomplice accused of trying to extort $40 million from entertainer Bill Cosby agreed on Tuesday to remain in prison until they can propose a bail package.

Autumn Jackson, 22, and Jose Medina, 51, of Ohio, were arrested on Saturday on charges they demanded money from Cosby to refrain from selling a tabloid newspaper a story alleging that Jackson is the entertainer's illegitimate daughter.
Federal prosecutors said there was no evidence the scheme was connected with the murder of Cosby's son Ennis last week.

Little information was released about Jackson and Medina as they were charged in a Manhattan court with conspiracy and extortion. If convicted they face a maximum prison term of seven years and fines of $500,000.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Andrew Peck appointed lawyers to represent them because they could not afford representation. Attorneys Robert Baum and Neil Checkman met briefly with their clients for the first time before the arraignment and neither would comment on the relationship between the defendants.
According to court papers, Jackson was one of many young people for whom Cosby paid educational expenses for several years. He has denied Jackson is his daughter.

Federal prosecutors said the alleged extortion scheme came to light after Cosby's lawyer told authorities Jackson and Medina were threatening to provide a tabloid newspaper with "certain information regarding Jackson being the daughter of Cosby" unless they received a payment of $40 million.

The lawyer contacted the Federal Bureau of Investigation and recorded three conversations in which Jackson said she was willing to accept a lower figure of $24 million to "end everything." Jackson and Medina were arrested at the lawyer's office after they signed an agreement for that amount.
According to court papers, the scheme began late last year when Cosby's lawyer received a telephone call from Jackson claiming to be Cosby's illegitimate daughter and stating she was "out of money."

The lawyer allegedly sent Jackson $3,000 on Cosby's behalf. Jackson then allegedly left messages at Cosby's home asking for more money. The lawyer returned the calls and said Cosby would pay only educational expenses.
